# md2pdf

> Free, no-login, client-side GitHub README to PDF converter and documentation workstation.

md2pdf (developed by LadeStack, founded by Girish Lade) converts public GitHub repositories and local Markdown files into print-ready PDF documents directly in the browser. All processing—fetching, Markdown parsing, HTML sanitization via DOMPurify, vector PDF layout with custom font embedding, and ZIP archiving—runs entirely within the browser sandbox with zero server uploads.

## Core Workflows & Capabilities

- **Single Document Engine**: Paste a GitHub repository URL, upload local Markdown files (`.md`, `.markdown`, `.txt` up to 2 MB), or edit in the browser with live debounced preview.
- **Documentation Book Builder**: Recursively scan GitHub repositories via the Git Trees API, select chapters using an interactive tree with tri-state checkboxes, reorder chapters, generate custom cover pages and hierarchical tables of contents, and print or export.
- **ZIP Export**: Bundle per-chapter PDFs into a single ZIP archive client-side using JSZip, preserving repository folder hierarchies and Unicode filenames.
- **Curated Print Themes**:
  - *Clean*: Neutral, modern sans-serif design for technical documentation.
  - *Business*: Serif display typography tailored for executive and client deliverables.
  - *Academic*: Justified layout and restrained styling for papers and course packs.
  - *Dark*: High-contrast screen preview with automated print legibility optimization.
- **Privacy & Security**: Zero server backend. No accounts, cookies, or remote tracking. All HTML is rigorously sanitized with DOMPurify to strip executable scripts and untrusted objects.
- **Browser-Local Storage**: IndexedDB auto-save (~1s debounce), automatic session restoration, versioned snapshots, full-text search, and JSON backup export/import.
- **Multilingual Support**: Fully localized into 9 languages: English (`/`), Spanish (`/es/`), Japanese (`/ja/`), Korean (`/ko/`), Simplified Chinese (`/zh/`), Russian (`/ru/`), Turkish (`/tr/`), French (`/fr/`), and Brazilian Portuguese (`/pt/`).

- [7 Practical Use Cases for Turning a README into a PDF](https://md2pdf.ladestack.in/blog/readme-to-pdf-use-cases/): Real-world workflows for client handoffs, release archives, course packs, engineering RFCs, and compliance snapshots.
- [GitHub README to PDF Converter](https://md2pdf.ladestack.in/blog/github-readme-to-pdf/): Direct repository import, branch resolution, and relative asset rewriting.
- [Multi-File Documentation Book Builder](https://md2pdf.ladestack.in/blog/multi-file-markdown-book/): Stitching multi-chapter Markdown handbooks with continuous page numbering.
- [Curated Print Themes](https://md2pdf.ladestack.in/blog/readme-pdf-print-themes/): Choosing print stylesheets, typography, and page setups.
- [Browser-First Privacy Architecture](https://md2pdf.ladestack.in/blog/browser-only-markdown-to-pdf/): Client-side security model and zero-upload guarantees.
- [Markdown Code Blocks to PDF](https://md2pdf.ladestack.in/blog/markdown-code-blocks-to-pdf/): Monospace code styling and print page-break containment.
- [Markdown Table of Contents](https://md2pdf.ladestack.in/blog/markdown-table-of-contents-pdf/): Auto-generating hierarchical TOCs for long documents.
- [Markdown ZIP Export](https://md2pdf.ladestack.in/blog/markdown-zip-pdf-export/): Packaging individual chapter PDFs into client-side archives.
- [Multilingual Unicode Fonts](https://md2pdf.ladestack.in/blog/multilingual-markdown-pdf-fonts/): Font embedding for Latin, Cyrillic, and CJK scripts.
- [About md2pdf](https://md2pdf.ladestack.in/about/): Project mission, founder Girish Lade, and LadeStack background.
